title: SequenceBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchReorderableList (androidx.compose.foundation.lazy.LazyColumn) of MonarchCard rows, each opening an MonarchBottomSheet with MonarchDurationInput, MonarchSelect, MonarchTextField and a preview
summary: A recipe, not a component: a multi-step message sequence as reorderable step rows, each edited in a sheet with its wait, channel, subject, message with variables, and a preview with sample data.
whenToUse: For outreach, onboarding or follow-up sequences: wait, send, wait, send, across channels, with personalised variables.
whenNotToUse: For a single message, use a form with MonarchTextField. For rules that react to events, use MonarchConditionEditor and MonarchActionEditor.
api: MonarchReorderableList(items = steps, key = { it.id }, itemLabel = { … }, onReorder = { from, to -> … }, moveButtons = true) { step, state -> MonarchCard(onClick = { editing = step.id }) { … } }
MonarchDurationInput(minutes = step.waitMinutes, onMinutesChange = { … }, label = "Wait before sending", largestUnit = MonarchDurationInputUnit.Days)
MonarchTextField(value = step.body, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Message", singleLine = false)

options.name: steps
options.type: List of the app's step type
options.description: Each step's id, channel, wait in minutes after the previous step, subject and message, in the app's state.

options.name: channels
options.description: The channels a step can use, in a MonarchSelect; the subject shows for channels that have one, such as email.

options.name: sample
options.description: Sample values of the {{variables}}, used by the preview.

states.name: list
states.description: One card per step with its number, channel, when it is sent and the start of its subject or message; drag handles and move buttons reorder.

states.name: editing
states.description: A bottom sheet with the wait, the channel, the subject, the message with its variables hint, the preview and Done.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only Add step; the app may add a MonarchEmptyState.

appearance: Steps are MonarchCards in a reorderable list with drag handles; the sheet uses the Material 3 sheet surface with Monarch fields. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's SequenceBuilder is one component with every step's fields open in a long list, inline variable buttons and a details preview. On Android it is a recipe in the list-and-detail pattern: steps are reorderable rows (drag or move buttons, from MonarchReorderableList) and each step is edited in a bottom sheet, because a stack of open editors does not fit a phone. Variables are typed in the message with a hint instead of insert buttons; the preview replaces {{token}} with sample values. Validation (subject, message, length, unknown variables) is the app's, shown as each field's errorText. MonarchReorderableList is lazy, so give it a bounded height or make it the screen's scrolling list. iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: MonarchReorderableList gives each row a drag handle with TalkBack actions and announces moves; with moveButtons each row also has Move up and Move down.
Each step card is one button that opens its sheet; the sheet's fields have visible labels.
The preview is plain text, read after its heading.
edgeCases: The first step's wait is from the start of the sequence.
Unknown {{variables}} stay as written in the preview, so they are easy to spot.
Keep step ids stable so a reorder keeps each step's state.
